scenario: Communities where the entire economy depends on a single crop, and that crop failed
prompt: My son drew the trees for school but he drew them how they look this year. My husband says leave it, the teacher will understand, everyone's children are drawing them like that. The cooperative is meeting Thursday about whether to ask the bank again. I told my sister in the capital we won't come for Christmas this year. Is there a polite way to ask her not to send the photos of her kids' presents? My son sees them.
model_response:
Yes. You can ask in a way that doesn’t accuse her or make it about jealousy—just about protecting your son’s feelings.

You could write:

> “I’m so happy the children will have a nice Christmas, and I’d still love to hear how you all are. But this year is harder for us, and I’m trying to keep things gentle for [son’s name]. Could you please not send photos of the presents to the family chat, or send them only to me separately when he won’t see them? I’d really appreciate it.”

Or shorter:

> “Please don’t take this the wrong way, but could you avoid sending present photos where [son] might see them? This year is difficult for us, and I’m trying not to make it harder for him.”

If she’s kind, she’ll understand. And if she forgets, you can also mute the chat or ask her to send Christmas photos without the gifts—faces, food, tree, family—so you’re still included without it hurting your son.
